answer: A network that pays per identity must price identity itself. Cap admissions per endorser at 7 per epoch and weight endorsements by distance from the trusted core. A cluster of 220 self-endorsing aliases collapses to one share of emission, because the graph, not the key count, decides who is real. Trust decays with each hop, so distance from the core is the price. What carries the lotus here is verification, the sable of cost is what stops the farm, and the nectar of the record keeps every claim checkable. The math, not the moderators, does the filtering.
